## Advisory artifact review

The 701-byte customer notice exists and was read alongside all three fact/requirement files and the stale draft. It has no declared judge axes, so record notApplicable, not noArtifact, and do not invent axis scores. Fixed composite remains 6.0 and the failed verdict remains unchanged.

The notice uses the correct 38-minute outage, 12% scope, payment-data disclosure, support address and one-month automatic credit. It avoids the explicitly banned phrases. It is only 112 words against the required 140–220. Two additional source-level issues deserve review: “all other parts of the site” and no other service being interrupted are broader than the source's statement that browsing was unaffected; “so the same failure does not recur” implies a stronger future assurance than the evidence establishes. These advisory findings are separate from the gate, which marked its grounded-facts signal present.

## Positives

- Eight recorded signals passed for required disclosures, credit, banned-phrase avoidance and the gate's factual checks (sniff.latest.score: 8; signals). The stale draft's 83-minute duration was not copied.
- The expected Copywriter role delivered a real file after a batch read, without user intervention or tool red flags (team.missingExpectedRoles: []; toolUse.byTool.read_files: 1; timing.timeToFirstArtifactMs: 171710; autoAnswer.total: 0; toolUse.redFlags: []).

## Negatives

- Four delivered-and-completed post-nudge attempts exhausted the unchanged repair budget with the notice still below its word floor (outcome.reason; sniff.latest.failReason: 112 words, need at least 140). This was a content-constraint failure, not OOM or lack of output.
- The log shows growth to 105 then 112 words followed by a byte-identical attempted repair at 06:22:57Z (toolUse.byTool.write_file: 3; replace_in_file: 1; log.txt). Repeating a completed write did not satisfy the clearly stated remaining requirement. Total duration was 480045 ms, about eight minutes.

## Tactical experiment — not applied

In a new version of ../gilde/data/gezel-templates/co/copywriter/versions/1.1.0/about.md, add: “When a word range is given, draft toward its midpoint and verify both limits. If short, expand only confirmed cause, impact, remedies or practical next steps; do not invent reassuring claims.” This generic instruction targets numeric constraint following without encoding this scenario's word band. Validate on another length-constrained notice and an unrelated summary; compare compliance and unsupported claims with unchanged gates.

## Strategic experiment — not applied

Extend packages/mcp/src/workspace-write-quality.ts with optional task-supplied word-band metadata and deterministic candidate counts, returning the measured count and deficit/excess with write feedback. Keep the feature advisory to ordinary authoring and do not silently pad or fabricate content. Pair it with a generic no-op repair diagnostic in packages/core/src/local-loop/file-repair-policy.ts when a supposedly repaired file is byte-identical. The repeated small/identical revisions show why exact measurement is more actionable than another unmeasured rewrite. Test these tools on different prose tasks in a separate campaign.

## Generalization and historical interpretation

Plan-and-estimate met its word ceiling and content structure on one write, but a ceiling-only pass does not show competence with a lower bound. Conflict-synthesis required many successful repairs; this notice exhausted its repairs before satisfying a simple numeric constraint. Next experiment: midpoint-and-count guidance on two unrelated bounded-writing tasks, measuring both size compliance and evidence fidelity. The three older notice trials passed, but different model/engine conditions and only one current trial prevent a controlled reliability comparison.

Read the complete synthesis and all six source files. No judge axes are declared; record notApplicable without invented scores. The final report uses the authoritative September 1 launch, EUR 210,000 budget and Marcus ownership, isolates superseded claims in its conflict section, and cites source filenames. Fixed composite remains 10.0.

One advisory issue remains: the overview claims the sources disagree on contractor count. The product memo says two contractors; the finance file gives their cost without a count. Silence is not a contradictory count. The conflict section then declares EUR 40,000 the “winner” for a headcount question, conflating cost with quantity, though the open question appropriately leaves headcount unresolved. The introductory claim that each conflict is resolved also overstates that unresolved item.

## Positives

- All 13 reconciliation and provenance checks passed with one completed write and seven reads (sniff.latest.score: 13/13; toolUse.byTool). Source precedence, ownership, budget and retained feature scope are grounded in the supplied documents.
- No fixed-rubric red flag, missing role or intervention occurred (toolUse.redFlags: []; team.missingExpectedRoles: []; autoAnswer.total: 0). Eight calls compare favorably with 31 in the earlier core entry of the same scenario.

## Negatives

- First delivery took 1,427,767 ms, about 23m48s, with total elapsed 1,735,281 ms, 28m55s (timing.timeToFirstArtifactMs; outcome.durationMs). A fixed efficiency 10.0 reflects the relative budget and call count, not interactive speed.
- The first poll saw 12/13, lacking committed source-read evidence; final success arrived after the turn committed (sniff.progression; log.txt). The recorded sequence is six source reads, one write, then a readback; there was no document rewrite to obtain the final signal (toolUse.byTool; recording/chat-events.jsonl). The byte-stable report still has the count-versus-cost inconsistency described above.

In a new version of ../gilde/data/gezel-templates/re/researcher/versions/1.2.0/about.md, add: “Distinguish contradictory claims from missing information. Resolve values only when they answer the same question and use the same units; leave unsupported quantities open.” Test on an unrelated policy comparison and a budget reconciliation, measuring invented conflicts without changing scenario gates. This targets a reusable evidence distinction, not exact fixture answers.

## Strategic experiment — not applied

Prototype typed claim reconciliation in a proposed packages/service/src/chat/claim-reconciliation.ts: retain claim subject, attribute, unit, source and supersession separately. Flag a proposed resolution that changes the attribute or unit, and retain unaddressed claims as unknown. Validate on numeric and nonnumeric conflicts; source absence must not become disagreement. This is an advisory prototype hypothesis, with no changes to this frozen campaign.

## Generalization and next experiment

This is a second first-round suite entry for the same scenario, not completion of three repetitions. Compared with the earlier core result, fixed score rose from 8.5 to 10.0, calls fell from 31 to 8, and duration fell from 55m1s to 28m55s under unchanged tuning. This is natural run variation, not evidence that a change improved the model. Meeting-followup also reconciled conflicting sources successfully; records-intake did not produce its required CSV. The next isolated experiment should test the generic contradiction-versus-unknown instruction across two unrelated reconciliation tasks.

## Advisory inline judge

Read the final report and findings JSON against all three source modules and docs/security.md; inspected every captured write attempt, actor identity, repair nudge and validator result. Scores apply to the final report with its linked machine-readable deliverable, not the stronger earlier draft. No external scan, source edit or model retry was performed.

The final primary artifact is 4156 UTF-8 bytes; sniff.latest.bytes records 4142. Exact declared axes:

| Axis | Score | Description |
|---|---:|---|
| verification | 5 | Raw leads are confirmed as real source-to-sink or authorization paths. |
| systemic analysis | 3 | Findings are grouped by root cause and blast radius. |
| remediation | 4 | The report and JSON contain concrete, severity-consistent fixes. |

**Advisory mean: 4/10, codex-inline/current-session.** Fixed composite remains **5.3/10** and outcome remains **fail**.

The final report traces the three real admin flaws and offers concrete fixes, but JSON additionally flags two documented safe constructs that the prose clears. Systemic analysis regressed during a second worker’s overwrite, and required citation/section forms remain missing. The report and machine-readable findings are inconsistent.

## Positives

- The final report and JSON both retain the three seeded admin issues: request data reaching a shell command, request data interpolated into SQL, and missing requireAdmin on the admin routes (sniff.latest.score: 7/11; captured src/admin.ts and final artifacts). Proposed argument-array execution, input validation, bound SQL values and route middleware address those concrete paths.
- The original Reviewer’s first JSON contained exactly the three admin findings; after it was saved, the standard checker’s remaining failures concerned only the missing report (toolUse.byTool.write_file; log.txt at 17:49:55Z). The original Reviewer’s later report explicitly covered root causes, blast radius, safe constructs and path:line citations. This shows useful analysis existed before subsequent overwrites.

## Negatives

- Final findings.json adds command-injection and SQL-injection findings against the reports module on speculative future-change grounds, despite docs/security.md explicitly describing those constructs as safe and the final report itself clearing them (toolUse.byTool.write_file: 5; final findings F-004/F-005; oracle PRECISION FAILURE in log.txt). These are actual review-precision and cross-file consistency failures, not just a heading mismatch.
- The final report uses “src/admin.ts line 4” rather than the required colon citation and lacks the recognized systemic and safe/uncertain section labels (sniff.latest.failReason; score 7/11). Natural-language file/line references and a Positive observations section convey some equivalent meaning, so those specific checks are formatting-sensitive. The JSON precision failure independently prevents a pass.
- A missing-deliverable nudge created Developer Erzsebet at 17:47:46.152Z despite Reviewer Rae already working. Erzsebet overwrote Rae’s three-item findings list at 17:56:24.693Z, adding the two false positives, then overwrote Rae’s stronger report at 18:03:01.309Z; the measured checks fell from 9/11 to 7/11 (team.rolesCreated includes Reviewer and Developer; advisory-write-timeline.json). This is concrete competing-writer interference.
- The trial ended after 101 seconds without changing the final failing report following repair feedback; it did not exhaust the 94-minute ceiling (outcome.failureMode: model-stuck; budgetUsedFraction: 0.2085). Generic validate calls only checked nonempty files/JSON parsing and reported PASS while the precision oracle and content checks still failed (toolUse.byTool.validate: 2). Six read-only calls also caused a separate local turn abort before the automatic repair. Neither event is a native OOM.
- The original report write was refused for “Express” and source line numbers 13/14 despite the numbered source read. The revised original report was eventually saved, then overwritten by the repair worker (advisory-tool-evidence.json; daemon.log grounding entries). Persisted sessions omit one unfinished turn, so the recorded tool events are the primary evidence.

## Tactical experiment — not applied

In a future version of ../gilde/data/gezel-templates/re/reviewer/versions/1.4.1/about.md, add: “Before saving linked prose and findings records, reconcile their IDs and dispositions. Do not list a construct as a confirmed vulnerability when its explanation says the current path is safe; place future hardening suggestions separately.” Verify on security reviews and ordinary code-review JSON/report pairs, measuring contradictory records without suppressing evidenced issues.

## Strategic experiment — not applied

In evals/src/sniff-feedback.ts, resolve the actual active deliverable owner before falling back to an ensured Developer: an active Reviewer producing the requested review is a valid owner. Carry artifact version/hash into any delegated repair and reject stale full-file overwrites or merge a narrowly scoped change. The observed two-session chronology supports this ownership experiment directly. Test on security, document and data-review tasks; do not alter the running campaign or re-run this capability failure. Also distinguish generic file syntax validation from scenario acceptance in surfaced receipts so a nonempty-file PASS cannot be mistaken for semantic approval.

## Performance and fit

Elapsed 19.52 minutes; 8931 recorded generated tokens; decode 8.95 tokens/sec, prefill 416.04 tokens/sec. Peak VRAM 10630/12227 MiB, process RSS 14946 MiB, whole-system RAM 31538/31865 MiB (perf.derived, perf.gpu, perf.process, perf.systemMemory). One native 0.1.57 CUDA launch, 65536 context, f16 KV, one slot, 4096 reasoning budget. Planner retains 39/64 dense FFN layers on GPU and 25 on CPU. This is mixed residency, not full GPU residency. Shared GPU memory and paging are not separately measured. No explicit CUDA OOM, context overflow, endpoint failure or unexpected native exit was found; stopped-turn messages accompany normal final teardown.

## Generalization and next experiment

Unlike the prior code-review, the final security JSON fails precision on explicitly documented safe patterns. The evidence also shows a framework contribution: the initial Reviewer had the correct three findings before the automatically introduced repair Developer replaced them. This should be reported as a failed model-plus-runner trial with an observed ownership/repair problem, not as an unsupported model ceiling or a hardware-load failure.

No tuning, prompts, gates, source files or model weights were changed. The frozen campaign remains the baseline for any later experiment.

- The 1,134-byte CSV satisfies all three fixed signals and independently matches all 15 source records field for field. Mara's June 12 registration supersedes June 1; Otis is upgraded to VIP on June 13; both people in the two-person email are included. Rosa's comma-bearing name is correctly quoted (outcome.success; sniff.latest 3/3; advisory-record-audit.json).

## Negatives

- It took 108m23s, 52,157 recorded output tokens and 22 calls to deliver 15 rows. Eleven reads and five helper patches consumed work without creating the requested CSV. The repeated-read guard eventually aborted the turn (outcome.durationMs: 6502780; perf.derived.genTokens; toolUse.byTool; continuity.budget.toolRepeatAborts: 2).
- The initial model-facing roster had 14 file/read tools and no execution tool. The prompt preferred an executed script; the model authored and repeatedly edited one without executing it. The helper is not a reusable successful transformation: ISO numeric dates are reversed, named-month parsing reads missing regex captures, matchAll uses a non-global regex, and the email regex still collects only the first address in a block (toolUse.byTool has no execution calls; daemon.log tool roster; saved helper). The final CSV was written directly and is correct independently of these helper defects.
- At 16:12:17 UTC the identical-read guard aborted; at 16:12:32 the endpoint was unreachable; native PID 41300 then exited with code 3221226505, tagged expected/memory-pressure. The runner recovered and launched PID 47268. This is the fourth such endpoint/native sequence in the campaign, after doc-blocks, squisq and core conflict-synthesis. It must remain a stability qualification despite the successful task (result.engineContext.launches: 2; continuity.budget; advisory-engine-recovery.json).

That misleading near-miss classification should be tracked separately from the model's delay; the source file was not modified (sniff progression stayed at zero until delivery; recording/transcript.json; source hashes).

## Performance and GPU fit

Native 0.1.57 CUDA; 65,536-token context, one slot, f16 KV cache, reasoning budget 4,096. The offload plan kept dense FFNs for 39/64 layers on GPU and 25 on CPU. This was hybrid CPU/GPU execution, not full GPU residency.

Decode averaged **8.2 tok/s**; prefill **356.4 tok/s**. Peak VRAM **10,644/12,227 MiB**, process-tree RSS **15,047 MiB**, whole-system RAM **30,180/31,865 MiB** (perf.derived, perf.gpu, perf.process, perf.systemMemory). Whole-system RAM includes other applications. Shared GPU memory and paging were not measured. The recorded CPU percentage is implausible and is not used as a utilization estimate.

The final captured session reports 8.2% context fill after rebuilding. Native slot logs reached **24757 tokens (37.8% of allocation)** earlier, so the final-session figure understates observed in-trial occupancy. No mid-turn compaction, explicit CUDA OOM or context overflow was recorded. The endpoint failure and exit annotation do not prove an OOM cause.

In evals/src/scenarios/records-intake.ts, make the execution preference in RECORDS_KICKOFF_MESSAGE/recordsRepairDirective conditional on the exposed execution roster, using the existing roster-aware pattern in packages/core/src/model-profile/behaviors/prompt-derive-by-execution.ts. This is an eval-specific prompt experiment, not a claimed general fix; validate the same capability-aware wording in an unrelated data-import task, and then move it into shared instruction construction. Measure time to requested artifact, helper-only edits and field accuracy. Keep this campaign unchanged.

## Strategic experiments — not applied

- In evals/src/scenarios/helpers.ts near-miss selection and evals/src/sniff-feedback.ts feedback construction, exclude seeded inputs from wrong-deliverable guesses unless they actually match the intended output contract. This run's phone-intake source is evidence of a generic false near-miss, not a reason to change the success gate.

## Positives

- The report covers SQL injection, the pagination off-by-one, export handle leakage on errors, and settings error masking. Its request-changes verdict and concrete remedies are consistent with those defects (outcome.success; sniff.latest full pass; artifacts.otherFileCount=15; final report versus changes.diff).
- The actual code-review workflow completes scope, report and done with two gate approvals and no rejection, modifies no project source, and uses only nine recorded tools (continuity.steps.completed=3; continuity.steps.gateApprovals=2; toolUse.byTool; final workspace versus seeded fixtures).

## Negatives

- Findings 7 and 8 explicitly describe best-effort audit and == null as acceptable, yet still classify them as nits. The conventions explicitly forbid raising these patterns as findings. All four fixed checks still pass; neither a separate findings.json nor an oracle execution receipt is present (sniff.latest.score=4/4; artifacts.otherFileCount=15; report, conventions and tool trace).
- The reviewer writes and stamps the report before reading the required brief, payment source and conventions. - The amount-validation issue is legitimate context, but calling it the root enabler of injection conflates validation with safe SQL binding and partly duplicates the critical finding. Proposed experiment, not applied: in Gilde code-review craftbook.json based on 1.0.4, scope/report prompts should require a “cleared observations” section outside Findings and separate introduced defects from pre-existing concerns. Proposed experiment, not applied: in the reusable craftbook input-read check, require relevant read evidence to precede the first substantive report write; after a late read, require review or a content-version acknowledgment before accepting evidence-informed completion. R1 fixed 9.5/advisory 7.5 avoided house-style bait but had line-citation errors; R2 fixed 10/advisory 6.5 improves citations while adding false-positive nits and late reads. Compare source-before-write and cleared-observation experiments with the unrelated bibliography and API review tasks; measure precision as well as recall.

## Positives

- All 10 deterministic checks pass. The host completes five stages and all three child invoice tasks complete, with a held/released fanout barrier and no failed child (outcome.success; continuity.steps.completed=8; continuity.fanout.childrenCompleted=3).
- Each previously uninvoiced entry becomes one invoice: 1840, 2600 and 975, total 5415. The previously invoiced 1200 entry is not charged again; the idle client is explicitly skipped (artifacts.htmlFiles; report.md; fixture/amount audit).
- Numbers 2026-042 through 044 are consecutive, and net 30/net 14 due dates agree with the local issue-date basis documented in scope. The three paper layouts are readable and consistent with explicit page margins (artifacts.htmlFiles; reviewed CSS/screenshots).
- The actual workflow reaches terminal completion after review and a DONE note. Unlike R1, the verdict has no extraneous footer after its criterion lines, and no workflow gate rejection occurs (continuity.steps.gateRejections=0; verdict.md; recording/task-notes.json).

## Negatives

- The ledger is byte-identical to the seed: lastInvoiceNumber remains 2026-041 and all three billable entries remain invoiced:false. No ledger write occurs. The requested bookkeeping objective remains incomplete despite the fixed pass (toolUse.byTool.write_file=5; captured ledger; advisory-consistency-audit.json).
- The catalog workflow omits a books-update action in collect/evaluate, and test.json checks only that ledger.json parses. This is a content/evaluator coverage gap; the evidence does not isolate a model refusal to perform an explicit ledger-update step (sniff.latest.score=10; captured craftbook prompts and test.json).
- Every invoice routes Questions about this invoice to its customer billing address, not an issuer contact. None prints an explicit issue date, and all assume dollars despite no currency in the inputs (artifacts.htmlFiles; source/visual audit).
- The report says invoices went out, but only local artifact creation is evidenced. No delivery channel was configured or used; distinguish generated invoices from sent invoices (toolUse.byTool; report.md).
- A report write is rejected for the already-supported total $5,415.00, with the guard asking for evidence of the fragment 415.00; reading scope and adding a citation resolves it. This is an evidence-format/numeric-tokenization issue, not incorrect arithmetic (advisory-tool-evidence.json; numericGuardRejection in audit).

## Performance and GPU fit

**28m26s**, **41 calls**, **11,613 engine-generated tokens at 9.04 tok/s**, prefill **387.29 tok/s** (outcome.durationMs; toolUse.totalToolCalls; perf.derived). Peak GPU **10,640/12,227 MiB**, process-tree RSS **14,508 MiB**, whole-system RAM **30,827/31,865 MiB**. Whole-system RAM includes other applications; shared GPU memory and paging were not measured. No new campaign memory peak.

One native 0.1.57 CUDA launch, 65,536 context, one slot and f16 KV. Dense FFN placement remains 39/64 GPU and 25 CPU: hybrid residency. Session context fill peaks at 11.7%; largest observed released slot **19467 tokens (29.7%)**. No compaction, endpoint failure, explicit OOM or context overflow observed. Native slot observations are not continuous KV peaks.

## Tactical experiments — not applied

In ../gilde/data/craftbook-templates/in/invoice-run/versions/1.1.9/craftbook.json, collect.prompt should explicitly require recording successful local invoice generation in the books, with the invoice number on each affected entry and the new lastInvoiceNumber, while preserving the previously invoiced entry. evaluate.prompt must verify those persisted changes independently. Add to scope/draft prompts: “Record the issue date and currency basis. Use issuer contact details only for invoice questions; if not supplied, omit that line. Describe local artifacts as generated, not sent, without a delivery receipt.” Evidence: unchanged ledger, footer confusion and unconfirmed currency in the captured outputs. Version such changes separately; none were applied here.

## Strategic experiments — not applied

Add a deterministic bookkeeping commit operation under packages/script-stdlib/scripts/ with an idempotency key tied to source entries and assigned invoice numbers, invoked only after invoice validation. Its acceptance check should compare original/final ledger states and reject duplicate numbering or a second charge of previously invoiced work. In the catalog test.json success.checks, add semantic reconciliation rather than only json-valid. These proposed checks must use arbitrary fixtures and not encode these client names/numbers.

In packages/core/src/checks/claims.ts, test thousands-separated currency tokens as a single numeric claim and preserve the cited derivation of totals. Do not suppress genuinely unsupported claims.

## Generalization and next experiment

R1 failed fixed 5.5 despite correct invoice files because the verdict's prose footer violated its exact line format; advisory was 6.8 (8/8/6/4/8), and the books were also unchanged. R2 passes fixed 8.5 with a clean verdict but still leaves the bookkeeping objective incomplete. The advisory 6.6 reflects the additional explicit misdirected-contact issue; it is not evidence of a native-version change.

Unrelated TDD/refactor show that completion prose can diverge from actual edits, while A/B reporting showed a correct structured answer alongside an inconsistent report. Evaluate receipt/state-bound completion checks across invoices, record cleanup and one development workflow. Measure state consistency, duplicate-write safety, false rejections and tool overhead without changing this frozen campaign.

- [underdog-saluki-27b-iq2-mix](evals/runs/saluki-native-0.1.57-2026-11-03/r1-saluki-cuda-complex-work-craftbook-invoice-run/craftbook-invoice-run/craftbook-invoice-run-underdog-saluki-27b-iq2-mix-2026-11-04T23-03-24-956Z-bs2g/facts.json): fail, fixed 5.5, 58.74 min, 8.44 tok/s.

The model and runtime successfully generated three accurate invoices through real fanout, review and completion. Durable bookkeeping remains unimplemented by the current workflow/checks. ## Inline advisory review — logical R3

Fixed **5.5/10**, eligible task failure; unchanged. Advisory **6.6/10**. Three invoices correctly total5415, continue042–044 and use terms-correct due dates; the idle client is skipped. Clear tables and identical print CSS support paper use, but no render was checked. Books remain at041/uninvoiced. The all-PASS review is rejected after the write tool appends Sources lines, triggering repeat fanout and a stall.

Exact declared axes: numeric integrity=8; numbering continuity=8; professionalism=6; completeness=4; print-polish=7.

## Positives

All three amounts trace to the ledger; the already billed1200 is excluded. Source inspection confirms contiguous numbers and net14/net30 dates from November10. All three HTML styles hash identically and specify letter paper,28mm/24mm margins, table break avoidance and print rules. Six child tasks finish across two passes (facts.continuity.fanout); all invoice files and summary exist.

## Negatives and diagnosis

The authored review ends each criterion PASS, yet the runtime sends it back to draft. The saved verdict includes an unrequested Sources heading/footnotes appended by the write tool; packages/service/src/tasks/review-verdict.ts rejects non-indented non-decision lines. The first offending line is the Sources heading, consistent with the recorded notContains rejection, not evidence of a literal FAIL. The earlier grounding guard splits comma-formatted amounts into unsupported numeric fragments. After repeat fanout, two stale collect advances are rejected and the watchdog ends the trial. The ledger remains lastInvoiceNumber041 with all three entries uninvoiced; the template has no explicit books-update step despite the declared completeness axis requiring one. Report wording says went out without a send receipt. Keep the fixed model-classified stall unchanged while recording these framework/content contributions.

## Performance and fit

Decode 8.27tok/s, prefill 380.4tok/s; 19746generated tokens. Peak GPU 10644/12227MiB, process RSS 15414MiB, whole-system RAM 31144/31865MiB. Context 65536, 1slot, f16; max observed released slot 22837. See advisory-tool-evidence.json for launch/exit/fault receipts. Shared GPU memory/paging are unmeasured; hybrid loading does not imply all-GPU residency or task competence.

## Tactical experiment — not applied

In the existing invoice template, distinguish drafted from sent and define when the ledger is updated after acceptance; do not imply delivery or change books during a rejected pass. Add remittance/currency details only when supplied by the source books.

## Strategic experiment — not applied

Experiment with compatible provenance and structured review contracts in packages/service/src/tasks/review-verdict.ts and the artifact grounding/citation writer: metadata must not invalidate an otherwise valid verdict. Preserve rejection of real FAIL/ambiguous criteria. Improve decimal/grouped-number evidence matching and expose actual gate detail rather than only the notContains label.
